discovery: Establishing molecular astrophysics: the physical and chemical processes that carry matter from interstellar clouds into planet-forming disks

nominees.name: Ewine F. van Dishoeck
nominees.affiliation: Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, the Netherlands

nominees.name: Alexander G. G. M. Tielens
nominees.affiliation: Leiden Observatory, Leiden University, the Netherlands, and University of Maryland, USA

subfield: Astrophysics / astrochemistry and star and planet formation
motivation: The nominees made molecules into precise physical probes of the Universe. Herbst showed that gas-phase ion-molecule reactions, driven by cosmic-ray ionization, explain the chemistry of cold interstellar clouds. Tielens developed the physics of photodissociation regions and grain-surface ice chemistry, and established that polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons dominate interstellar infrared emission. Van Dishoeck quantified molecular photodissociation and radiative transfer, and led the observational programmes with ISO, Spitzer, Herschel, ALMA and JWST that followed water, ices and complex organic molecules from dense cores through protostars into planet-forming disks. Their combined theory, laboratory-informed physics and observations turned spectral lines into quantitative diagnostics of temperature, density, ionization and time. They showed that the chemistry of planetary systems, including our own, is partly inherited from the interstellar medium. This work underpins modern star- and planet-formation physics and our understanding of cosmic origins.
